shortName: University of California, San Diego School of Medicine
additionalCoursework:
UC San Diego does not have requirements regarding coursework that must be completed. The following courses are recommended to make our evaluation of your application easier, and to better prepare you for the MCAT and for medical school:

One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Biology
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level General Chemistry
One term (1 semester or 1 quarter) of college-level Biochemistry
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Organic Chemistry.
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Physics.
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Calculus or Statistics
Laboratory coursework for all courses that offer corresponding labs.

Applicants that are missing any of these courses will still be considered.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The UCSD School of Medicine is committed to expanding the educational opportunities for applicants coming from disadvantaged educational or economic backgrounds. This institutional commitment is expressed through a pre-matriculation summer program, a conditional acceptance program, educational support programs, and financial aid assistance. The Office of Diversity and Community Partnerships supports innovative programs that enhance the academic, clinical, scholarly and advocacy skills of middle school, high school, community college, undergraduate, post-baccalaureate, graduate and medical students. More information on these programs is available at: https://medschool.ucsd.edu/education/diversity/Pages/default.aspx
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may have compelling reasons for slowing their progress through the curriculum and/or taking a leave of absence. Students may request (or be required) to take a reduced course load or to take a leave from the curriculum for a variety of reasons.  Leaves of absence are typically taken either for personal reasons or because the student is involved in a year long research, service, and/or global health program.  Permission for such leaves are granted by the Associate Dean for Undergraduate Medical Education.  Counseling is provided to students regarding the financial aid implications of a leave of absence.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Medical students engage their community and complement their medical education, training, and experience through a variety of leadership positions, student organizations, professional associations, and medical interests groups. With 30 elected and appointed leadership positions and over 40 active student organizations, UCSD medical students have myriad opportunities to grow through service activities, professional development, and community involvement. Medical student health and wellness are an integral component to professional competence. By offering a variety of programs focused on social, emotional, physical, spiritual, and intellectual development, UCSD medical students strive for balance and health in their lives as they pursue their medical degree. Detailed information regarding student organizations, societies, activities and athletics is available at https://medschool.ucsd.edu/education/undergrad/student_affairs/student_life/Pages/default.aspx
medSchoolStudLife.setting: UCSD School of Medicine is located in La Jolla, California.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Medical students at UCSD live both in on and off-campus housing. A description of on campus housing options is accessible at https://hdhgradfamilyhousing.ucsd.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The support of our gender and sexual minority students starts in Orientation Week, which includes a session on our LGBTQ+ community. We offer guidance and fiscal support to our active LGBTQ student organization for well-attended, school-wide events, such as a “Rainbow Pin Ceremony”, Transgender Week of Visibility, and National Coming out Day, and attendance at an annual Southern California LGBTQ Conference.  We help our students to create community with faculty and each other through events such as an annual Health Sciences LGBT mixer, and connect them with undergraduate campus LGBT resources. 

Our commitment to an inclusive and culturally humble community extends to our curriculum, which includes meaningful electives co-developed with students (an example of which is an “Intersections of LGBTQ Health Elective”), panel discussions by LGBQT health providers, and a Health Equity Thread in which all of our students learn about health inequities in sexual and gender minority communities.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Wellness and success is at the center of the person-centered student support approach in our Office of Student Affairs. Our students are supported through access to formal counseling and psychological services, access to on-site individualized mental health support, wellness-based programming and events, and facilitated peer support. The School of Medicine maintains a specific director position, recently elevated as the Director of Wellness Initiatives, who provides mental health support to individual medical students through weekly office hours, provides consultation on wellness event programming and opportunities for connectedness and belonging, and is responsible for providing the direction, management and innovative growth of wellness support and initiatives in our school. 

https://medschool.ucsd.edu/education/undergrad/student_affairs/wellness-success/Pages/default.aspx
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
UC San Diego School of Medicine is built on values that promote respect, justice, compassion, empathy and inclusion. We celebrate a culture of acceptance and collaboration where all members of our community are valued and respected. We believe that our equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) principles benefit not only our learning community, but also improve overall patient care and promote medical and research advancements.

EDI principles serve as cornerstones for all educational opportunities at UC San Diego School of Medicine. Future health care providers are trained to practice in underserved communities through EDI-guided educational programs designed to address health inequities.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Casual dress is permitted during the first two years, except when students are working with patients.  Professional dress is required for all clerkships and episodic interactions with patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Educational Support Services (OESS) at UCSD School of Medicine strives to improve students' comprehension and retention of information in the preclerkship curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interaction during the fall quarter of their first year through the Clinical Foundations course and the ambulatory care apprenticeship.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The integrated scientific curriculum in the first two years utilizes lectures, small groups, laboratory sessions, and self-directed learning modalities.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: The required third year rotations include internal medicine, general surgery and surgical subspecialties, pediatrics, neurology, psychiatry, and obstetrics-gynecology.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: A seven week prematriculation program is available  during the summer preceding the start of medical school.  https://medschool.ucsd.edu/education/md-combined/curriculum/oess/ctbs/index.html
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Students are encouraged to attend lecture; attendance is recorded at small groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The goal of the medical curriculum and faculty-student interactions is to develop critical, objective, conscientious physicians prepared for changing conditions of medical practice and continuing self-education. The new integrated scientific curriculum utilizes a systems based approach to provide a solid foundation in the various scientific disciplines basic to medicine. Students are introduced to patient care in the outpatient setting from the beginning of their first year.  The core curriculum of the last two years is composed of the major clinical specialties taught in hospital and out-patient settings, and relevant extended-care facilities. Elective opportunities are pursued during both the pre-clinical and clinical years.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Medical students at the UCSD School of Medicine are introduced to Primary Care during the fall quarter of year one, through the Ambulatory Care Apprenticeships, a part of the Clinical Foundation core course.  This program allows students to work in the outpatient practice of a primary care physician for one afternoon every other week. The apprenticeships continue through the first five quarters of medical school.  During the third year, every student is required to complete the Primary Care core clerkship.  In this clerkship, students work for one afternoon every week in the outpatient practice of a primary care physician.  Finally, during the fourth year, one of the required direct patient care clerkships is one month of a primary care clerkship.  This can be selected from a list of elective opportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students at the UCSD School of Medicine have access to a plethora of research opportunities both at UCSD and a number of other research institutions in La Jolla.  Approximately 40-60 students participate in research activities in the summer between year one and year two of medical school. These mentored research activities are supported by several different training grants available for short term student support and by institutional funds. For some students, these summer experiences lead to an interest in participating in a yearlong research program, typically funded by organizations such as the HHMI, the NIH, the Sarnoff Foundation, or the Doris Duke Charitable Trust.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: The vast majority of students participate in optional community service events.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: The School has a requirement for an independent study project and research is one way to complete this.  Basic, translational and clinical research opportunities are available for medical students.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Medical student education and training takes place at all UCSD hospitals, as well as multiple other affiliated sites within San Diego County (VA, Naval MC, and several Scripps hospitals).
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/fail during first two years.  Honors/High Pass/Pass/ Fail during third year clerkships.  Honors/Pass/Fail during fourth year clerkships.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Students at the University of California, San Diego (UCSD) benefit from a diverse faculty and access to a wide variety of research and clinical opportunities.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the UC San Diego School of Medicine is to provide skilled, compassionate physicians well-trained to practice medicine who are sensitive to the needs of the special populations of our region and the nation. In addition, we strive to build on our exceptional biomedical, behavioral and health services research strengths to extend the boundaries of the art and science of medicine through continued research and the preparation of future academicians. In these ways, we also strive to improve the overall health of the population.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: A single "Committee Letter" can be submitted in lieu of the minimum of 3 letters.  Letters from faculty who have worked more closely with the student tend to be more helpful to the committee.  It is helpful if 1-2 letters come from individuals who have supervised the applicant in an activity designated by the applicant as "most meaningful" on their AMCAS application.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letters from faculty at your four-year undergraduate institution are welcomed but not required. Letters can come from any source, including but not limited to: course instructors, research mentors, clinical faculty, work supervisors, non-faculty practicing physicians.  There are no requirements regarding sources of letters (e.g. you are not required to have a specific number of "science" vs "non-science" letters.    IF YOU ARE APPLYING TO THE MD/PHD PROGRAM, PLEASE NOTE THAT A MINIMUM OF TWO LETTERS SHOULD BE FROM RESEARCH-RELATED FACULTY
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: All sessions will be run via Zoom video conferencing.   Students receive a orientation at 8 AM in the morning.  MMI interviews occur until noon.  Applicants have a 1 hour Q & A session with current medical students, and then debrief with admissions staff.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: In August of the year preceding matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: The 4-year M.D. program, PRIME-HEq, PRIME-TIDE, and GHAC programs utilize Multiple Mini Interviews with faculty and 4th-year medical students.   The MD-Phd program utilizes both one on one and Multiple Mini Interviews.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: For the 2026-2027 application cycle, UCSD plans to use only remote video interviews (via Zoom)
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: The deadline is one month after the applicant is invited to submit the secondary application
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: There is no required relationship to the school or state for non-resident applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Coursework from Canadian universities is accepted.  Applicants still must meet our criteria re: citizenship as detailed in the "International Applicants" section
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: The UCSD SOM will consider applicants from US citizens, permanent residents of the US (green card), and DACA recipients. Applicants that do not satisfy one of these requirements won't be considered
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
TRANSFER STUDENTS

UC San Diego School of Medicine does not accept students in transfer from other medical schools.

---

CITIZENSHIP REQUIREMENT 

The UC San Diego School of Medicine will consider applications from U.S. citizens, permanent residents of the U.S. (green card holders), and DACA recipients. Applicants that do not satisfy one of these three eligibility requirements will not be considered.

---

COURSEWORK RECOMMENDATIONS

It is recommended that students enter medical school after four years of undergraduate study; the absolute minimum requirement is attendance for three academic years at an accredited college of arts and sciences, with at least one full year at an accredited 4-year institution in the United States. Students who have attended a foreign school must have completed at least one year of study at a four-year college in the United States prior to applying.  Exceptions may be made for students from Canadian schools - please contact somadmissions@ucsd.edu to inquire.

UCSD does not have requirements regarding coursework that must be completed. The following courses are recommended to make our evaluation of your application easier, and to better prepare you for the MCAT and for medical school:

One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Biology
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level General Chemistry
One term (1 semester or 1 quarter) of college-level Biochemistry
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Organic Chemistry.
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Physics.
One academic year (2 semesters or 3 quarters) of college-level Calculus or Statistics
Laboratory coursework for all courses that offer corresponding labs.

Applicants that are missing any of these courses will still be considered.

---
Policy regarding Pass/No Pass and On-Line coursework due to COVID-19 impact

The UCSD School of Medicine will accept, without prejudice, grades of Pass/No Pass for all coursework for Winter 2020, Spring 2020, the entire 2020  - 2021 academic year, and Summer 2021     For coursework outside of these time frames, Pass/No Pass are accepted but we would not recommend more than one course per academic year be taken Pass/No Pass.

We have always accepted grades from on-line courses and will continue to do so.

---

MCAT Policy – updated February 2026

MCAT "Expiration":  We will accept MCAT scores from January 2023 through December 2026.   Applicants that only have scores from prior to 2023, we will consider exceptions on a case-by-case basis.  Please contact somadmissions@health.ucsd.edu and include your MCAT scores.

We will not consider MCAT scores taken in early 2027

Applicants will not be invited to submit a secondary application unless they have an MCAT score available

 For all applicants, we will make decisions regarding interviews without consideration of the MCAT score (i.e. the MCAT score will be hidden from the applications that our screeners will review)    

 If an applicant was able to sit for an MCAT exam but feels their MCAT performance or ability to take the MCAT was significantly adversely affected by a pandemic-related issue, we will allow a short statement describing that hardship or adversity to be appended to their secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We will primarily consider the highest MCAT scores, but all lifetime scores are available to the committee
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: If an applicant doesn't maintain a 3.1 GPA in postbacc coursework, our committee is unlikely to invite them to interview
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Any number of post-bacc or graduate courses will be noted and will technically be considered.   However,  it is recommended that at least 1 academic year of full time coursework be taken
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: At the UCSD School of Medicine, we understand there are many valid reasons why an applicant would take coursework at a community college.   Any and all community college coursework is accepted by our committee.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants are permitted to submit corrections to UCSD regarding their AMCAS application if they discover they've made an error after they've submitted.   But we do not accept updates regarding new grades, new activities, or other accomplishments

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial aid in the form of scholarships, grants, loans, and work opportunities is offered to help students in need of financial assistance. Medical Scientist Training Program participants may receive full tuition and stipend support during their combined degree training.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Fees and tuition at the UCSD School of Medicine are determined annually by the Regents of the University of California in a process that seeks input from each School and Campus.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are typically informed of the admission committee's decision on their application within six weeks of their interview.  Those on the waitlist are re-evaluated for possible admission.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Recommended coursework is described at:  http://meded.ucsd.edu/index.cfm/asa/admissions/application_process/.  The School of Medicine will consider other means by which students may have demonstrated competency in the listed recommended coursework.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: This is not applicable to our school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee selects applicants who have demonstrated intelligence, maturity, integrity, and dedication to the ideal of service to society. The school is seeking a student body with a broad diversity of backgrounds and interests. The Admissions Committee seeks students with broad training and in-depth achievement in a particular area of knowledge, whether in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences. Other evaluation factors include evidence of meaningful involvement in extracurricular activities, performance on the MCAT, letters of recommendation, and personal interviews. The Admissions Committee interview evaluates the applicant's abilities and skills necessary to satisfy the non-academic or technical standards established by the faculty and the personal characteristics necessary to become an effective physician. Preference is afforded to applicants who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The School recognizes that it can be difficult for premedical students to obtain shadowing opportunities.  The School also believes that applicants are able to obtain realistic information about a career in medicine through many different types of experiences.  Volunteer work in a clinical setting, working as a scribe or medical or nursing assistant, or having a sustained level of involvement in community service are all experiences that can help to inform applicants regarding their own suitability for a career in medicine.
